commits.message:
Read the drill's chain transactions one Ogmios session at a time

Every confirmed-transaction read on an attached stack opens its own
Ogmios chain-sync session, and each session is a new node-to-client
connection to the stack's cardano-node. Callers ask for several reads at
once, and a burst of them overflowed the node's socket backlog: Ogmios
dropped the websockets it could not connect, and the drill failed a family
on "Ogmios chain-sync socket closed".

The reader now runs its reads one at a time, in the order they were asked
for. A failed read rejects only its own caller; the next one still runs.

Resume a completed withdrawal from its recorded payout

A resumed run reconciled every completed step again, and the withdrawal
step proved its payout by finding the payout output unspent at the L1
node's tip. A later cycle's deposit spends that output, so a resume after
cycle 1 waited out the full timeout and failed. Inclusion proven at depth
is permanent: a complete record that holds this withdrawal's payout (same
event, address and assets) is now taken as the proof, and only the L2
spend, the balance guard and readiness are checked again.

Select three more checks from the files they read

Three preflight checks read files their triggers did not name, so a change
to one of those files passed preflight unchecked:

- workflow-lint lints the composite actions under .github/actions/ as well
  as the workflows.
- agent-enforcement-tags resolves [eslint] tags against the ESLint configs,
  [ci] tags against the workflows' step names and [hook] tags against
  .githooks/.
- registry.mjs imports onchain/aiken/scripts/guard-focused-selector.mjs,
  which imports complete-test-shards.mjs, so both are preflight's own code
  and now full-run paths beside scripts/preflight/**.

Closes #947

Select the tooling self-tests from the files they read

repo-tooling-tests ran only on changes under scripts/, .githooks/ and
.claude/settings.json, yet several of its self-tests hold files outside
scripts/ to each other: the journey wiring check reads the watcher journey
tests and Node CI's workflow. A new journey test therefore passed preflight
and failed Repo Tools CI after the push.

Each self-test that reads files outside scripts/ now declares them in
toolingTestInputs, and the step is selected from those declarations. A
change to a declared file runs only the self-tests that read it; a change
under the step's own paths, a full run and `--run repo-tooling-tests` still
run the whole suite.

registry.tooling-inputs.test.mjs pins the selection and runs each declaring
self-test in a copy of the repository holding only scripts/ and the files it
declares, so a read left off its entry fails there, as does a glob that
matches no file. A self-test with no entry at all is not caught: whoever
adds a self-test that reads outside scripts/ adds its entry.

Refs #947

Wait out public DA's not_found after a block commits

The node reports a transfer committed before it hands the block's payload
to the committee, whose store the public retained-DA server reads. The
journey's transfer step fetched that payload once, so a fetch landing in
between failed the run with not_found although the payload arrived seconds
later.

The fetch now asks again while every attempt answers not_found, within the
step's existing limit, reusing one retained-DA runtime, and throws the same
error with the last attempts when the limit runs out. Any other answer
(conflict, invalid content, refusal, failed verification, transport error,
timeout) still fails at once.

Run the new drill harness journey tests in node CI

Five watcher-journey test files added with the drill harness fixes need no
devnet but were missing from the node CI list, so the wiring check failed.

State what an unspent seed row proves at a point

A seed row reads unspent while no spend at or below the point is
recorded. It may also cover an output created after the origin while its
wallet was untracked, so it does not prove the output existed at a point
before its seed slot.

Test a recorded release replaced by a rollback, and its settle boundary

Two cases on the real follower store read a release from its recorded block once the store has pruned the walk from the Open. In the first, a rollback replaced the recorded block and the same burn landed again at the same slot; the row is revived, not settled. In the second, the row stays unsettled at a depth of exactly automatic rollback recovery and settles one block later.

Test the availability reconcile's pending demotion and new-step pin

An included intent that a rollback took out of the store, together with
the blocks that created its inputs, now has a case showing it returns to
pending while still valid. A newly actuated step now has a case showing
its own submit pins it in the follower before it is broadcast, since the
pass pinned the journal before the step was signed.

Read availability inputs as unspent without needing their bytes

The availability reconcile asked the follower for the exact bytes of every
input of a signed intent that had not landed, only to learn which were
unspent. A wallet coin the follower's origin already held has no stored
creating transaction, so that read was refused and the whole pass failed
on every tick.

The follower now answers which outrefs are unspent at a point without
reading bytes: a seed row is unspent from the origin until a spend the
store records at or below the point. The byte read is built on the same
walk and still refuses where bytes are needed and absent. The intent
observation, the workflow release spend lookup and the signed-recovery
missing-row check use the new read.

End the funding test's families with a conviction

The last family's conviction needs no further bond. With a refused family
last, counting that bond or not gave the same total, so the test could not
tell. Ordering the attested family last makes an over-count refuse the
exactly-funded case.

Disarm every operator-2 release guard before the compose test's holder ends

A test that failed before its own release left the guard armed, so once
the fake docker directory was gone the guard could start a real compose
project. The teardown now releases every hold while the fake docker is
still first on PATH.

Settle availability workflow releases after the follower prunes

A released challenge workflow settles only once its terminal step is
deeper than automatic rollback recovery, and every release check walked
from the Open's node output. The follower keeps rows only to its
retained depth, which is far shallower, so that walk lost its first
rows long before the release could settle: the row deferred on every
pass and stayed in the journal, where it holds the wallet's capital.

The release pass now pins each terminal step before the journal records
it, and the journal's pin set keeps every unsettled release's terminal.
When the walk from the Open is no longer retained, the check re-reads
the recorded release from the block it was verified in: it stands while
that block is canonical and is revived once that block leaves the
chain. A walk that meets a pruned node output reads that output's spend
from the header's queue history, which the follower keeps while the
header is queued, checked against the spending transaction's own bytes.

Where nothing retained proves a release, the row stays live or
unsettled and its deferral carries the release-evidence-beyond-retention
reason instead of an unexplained refusal. Nothing is settled or dropped
without proof.

Count every operator-2 and funding spend in the drill's funding check

The funding check counted one bond per attested family and three fees
plus a header node per family. It left out the ledger owner's deposit
from the funding wallet, the user events (deposits, withdrawal and tx
orders) and history blocks that families stage from operator-2's
wallet, and the bond that a family after the last attested one posts
again.

It now takes the families in order and counts, from the constants the
spends use:
- the bond at the first family's onboarding (operator-2 may start
  unbonded, as after a run that ended in a conviction) and again for each
  family that follows a conviction;
- each family's onboarding and top-up fees, and its fault's header node;
- each history block's header node and commit;
- each user event at the deposit's amount (JOURNEY_USER_EVENT_LOVELACE,
  now the deposit's own constant) and its fee;
- the ledger owner's deposit (journey.depositLovelace) and its fee.

Fixtures now expose the history blocks and user events they declare;
the transition trace declares its two deposits and its empty block.

Read the verified-predecessor check's first tail read through a reset

The check's first read of the stack's attested tail was the one read
that a lost connection did not retry, so one reset closed the session
for every remaining family. It is now read again after a transport
failure (isTransientTransportError), pausing between tries, within the
check's existing decision bound on the check's own clock; at the bound
the last transport failure is rethrown. readThroughTransportFailures
takes an optional clock for this; its other callers keep the monotonic
clock.
